## Inputs on the Building Physics worksheet {#building-physics-inputs}

**Scope:** Keep construction, thermal boundary and heat flows distinct. Component assignment, the balance boundary and qualitative heat-flow overlays can be considered separately.

**Excel location:** [🧱 Bauphysik]{.excel-menu .darkred} worksheet.

::: {.excel-operation}
### In the Excel tool
| Input group | Assignment |
|---|---|
| Opaque thermal envelope | External walls excluding windows, roof or top-floor ceiling, basement ceiling / ground-contact floor; areas and U-values |
| Transparent elements | Window areas including frames by orientation, U- and g-values |
| Thermal bridges / airtightness | Allowance and n50 assumption based on project information |
| Shading / movable solar protection | Reduction factors and control assumptions; distinguish defaults from adopted values |
| Thermally active mass | Construction type and effective heat capacity |

Apply [quick selections](presets.qmd) first, then check project-specific areas and properties. After recalculation, review the heat balance on the [Results](results.qmd#heat-balance) worksheet.
:::

The section view locates the balance boundary in the building. [Life-cycle assessment](climate.qmd) also includes constructions within that boundary, so thermal envelope area and LCA quantity are not interchangeable.

## Visual style and technical layers

The **teaching** style reduces surroundings and decoration while retaining the section renderer's geometry. Component colours, thermal boundary, selection and heat flows are independent overlays. Existing styles remain available for other uses.

## Two thermally decoupled zones

The selector shows the cooled and uncooled zones individually; the two storeys do **not** represent these zones. Heating is possible in both, active cooling only in the cooled zone, and night ventilation in the illustrated reference model only in the uncooled zone.

Solar gains enter through windows; internal gains arise within the space. Transmission and ventilation are shown as example heat removal, but their direction depends on operating conditions. Arrows are **qualitative**; their width does not encode heat flow magnitude.

## Boundary of internal ceilings

The thermal envelope and component assignment illustrate different boundaries.

<details><summary>Thermal boundary conditions</summary>An internal floor slab between two heated storeys is within the thermal boundary. A slab above an unheated basement may form part of the thermal envelope. The thermal boundary condition matters, not only the geometric type “slab”. The <a href="components.qmd">second reference geometry</a> illustrates this distinction.</details>

::: {.callout-note}
## For a declaration
Internal heat gains and plug loads can be varied in the model. Use the designated declaration values of the relevant tool version for the declaration.
:::

Source: [Training, slides 11–14](../downloads/schulung.pdf). The geometry is an explicitly assumed reference building, not a project result.
